reference: Native CPython 3.14 with google-adk 2.12.0 (its own Runner, a scripted BaseLlm and a native tool)
requestReference: The native lane maps ADK's LlmRequest to OpenAI-format messages and tools in tests/conformance/cases-adk-python/native.py; the galaxie mapper is independent
lanes: real headless Chromium Pyodide (plain-text, capability, abort, stream-text, stream-abort, confirm-approve)
normalizations: Provider call IDs are runtime-generated on each side (ADK uses adk-<uuid>, galaxie uses galaxie-<n>), so request messages number them by first appearance.

Transcripts compare the requests the model saw, the scripted replies it returned, the capability calls, the run output and the run error. ADK events are not part of a transcript except the stream events a streaming case records: checked text deltas as `messages` and content-free tool markers as `updates`.

The native lane implements the capability tool itself with the same declaration, so the lanes compare the model mapping and the run loop, not the tool body. The denial case pins the fixed model-visible error a denied capability returns.

The native lane emulates the router's step budget (budget_exceeded before the third dispatch with a limit of two), the host output-safety block (denied) and cancellation, because it has no router; the lanes compare the observable outcome.

The native lane streams with ADK's SSE mode and a scripted model that yields word-sized partial responses (the router's mock splits the same way); the stream-mid-block case stops at the first chunk whose growing text holds the blocked marker, as the router's output check does, and stream-abort cancels after the first chunk.
ADK ends a cancelled root node quietly; the native fixture records the cancellation itself, and the galaxie run reports cancelled through the adapter.

The native lane drives pauses itself the way ADK documents them: a confirmation run ends after ADK's own `adk_request_confirmation` request and the answer is a new run with a `FunctionResponse` for that request; a long-running run is left after the call's pending result and the answer is a new run with a `FunctionResponse` for the call. Interactions carry the author hook's projection with positional requests `{kind, tool, args}`; ADK call IDs never appear. The interaction IDs are the fixture's `pause-<n>` names.

The native lane validates the default resume itself (approve or deny, every request covered once) and raises the fixed `invalid` and `stale` errors where the galaxie lane rejects the answer before any tool runs; the native `confirm-stale` and `confirm-double-submit` results are fixed expectations, and only the Worker lane produces the core's rejection codes. Pause markers (`paused`, one per request, tool name and position only) are content-free and restart their numbering with each run.

Stage AP5 stores a conversation as an adk-python.session/v1 record: the event log in the checkpoint and the per-session integrity key, pause counter and pending request in the metadata. One record travels in one 1 MiB bridge frame, so the executor projects the record size at every appended event and fails unsupported before the next model or tool dispatch; a start inside the margin is refused. Failed and cancelled runs write nothing, and partial events and binary parts are never stored. Restore is covered by tests/conformance/adk-python-restore.node.test.ts, not the golden cases, because it needs a second runtime lifetime.

Stage AP6 shape cases script the model by agent: a request is attributed to the agent named in ADK's system instruction (Your internal name is ...), and the reply is the agent's next entry after its own earlier assistant turns. The galaxie lane builds a fresh MockChatModel per call from that entry, so usage, tool offering and streaming chunking come from the same mock.

agents-parallel runs two branches concurrently, so its transcripts sort requests by agent and turn, responses by agent and per-agent turn, and capability calls by value before comparing; tool-call IDs are numbered per request. The right branch's final answer waits for the left branch's (an `after` gate in both lanes) so the merger agent sees one branch event as its last context in every run.
subgraphs stays false: ADK sub-agent events carry author and branch, not LangGraph namespaces, so galaxie exposes no nested stream paths or nested-pause parity.

shapes.pausing: A confirmation or long-running tool can pause only in a leaf agent that is the last child under every ancestor, and every ancestor must be a SequentialAgent. agents-confirm-last pauses and resumes in the last child of a SequentialAgent (also reloaded in tests/conformance/adk-python-restore.node.test.ts).

refusedAtPrepare.Workflow: Native ADK 2.12.0 runs it (final text 'step done'); the executor fails unsupported at prepare.
refusedAtPrepare.AgentTool: Native ADK runs the nested agent (root, worker, root); the executor fails unsupported at prepare.
refusedAtPrepare.pause inside ParallelAgent: Native ADK resumes only the paused branch and never runs the agent after the fan-out; unsupported at prepare.
refusedAtPrepare.pause inside LoopAgent: Native ADK ends the run after the first pass and never starts the next iteration; unsupported at prepare.
refusedAtPrepare.pause in a non-last SequentialAgent chil: Native ADK never runs the siblings after the paused child; unsupported at prepare.
refusedAtPrepare.pause in a transfer target: Native ADK resumes the target in place; refused at prepare because the transferring agent's state is not restored.

shapes.evidence: tests/conformance/cases-adk-python/test_adk_python_refused_shapes.py records the native results; tests/conformance/adk-python-agents.node.test.ts asserts the Worker refusals and the parallel write replay.
